historical_references.reference: The Mahabharata, an ancient Indian epic, mentions a king named Hrutik, who was a contemporary of the Pandava prince Bhima. Hrutik was a king of the Vaisya (merchant) community in the kingdom of Khandava. Bhima once visited Hrutik's kingdom and was impressed by his wealth and hospitality.

The Puranas, a set of ancient Hindu texts, describe Hrutik as a king of the Haihayas, a Yadava (Jain) dynasty. Hrutik is said to have ruled over the region of Mathura in present-day Uttar Pradesh, India. According to the texts, Hrutik was a just and wise ruler who was revered by his subjects.
